svg.title: SkySEED — complete system architecture
svg.desc: Authored inputs, Emulator, pure simulation, chronological production, BPF execution and separately owned evidence. Nested groups show ownership; blue arrows transfer values, dashed purple arrows call or control, and diamond lines hold objects.
svg.text: SkySEED / FROM AUTHORED SCENE TO OBSERVED NETWORK
One system, explicit owners and three kinds of evidence
Read top to bottom. Cards select real interfaces; a card is not necessarily a process.

g.text: Satellite input: Shells, orbit epoch / phase,
GS input: sites, coordinates, access limits
Explicit SEED layers, ASs, IXs and peering
AS holds EmulatorShell and GS objects
SEED nodes remain on this side of adapter

svg.text: _definition; owns _physical_world, _physical_link_model and _planner. Explicit create_physical_world(), create_planner(), shutdown().

g.text: Query result refers to this same timestamp
No operational state or timeline cursor
facts; calculation and runtime stay separate
Then compile_bpf for the Compiler cutoff
results/compiler/: binary Runner artifact, manifest, material references, execution.json
results/experiment/completed.json: one atomic request boundary and bounded stream prefixes
SEED build contexts and Docker Compose

svg.text: The three cards below are responsibilities of Runner, not three public classes.

g.text: _TcBpfRuntimeRealization + _PrivilegedHelper: netns FDs, sockets, veths, qdiscs, BPF maps / programs
Traffic probe plans are execution inputs
Tools read one completed byte prefix
A published request does not terminate
Relative browser assets, no Model replay
Runtime reads wait for completed invocation
Presentation can lag; failure preserves facts
Active tool owns probes and telemetry
Runner owns network state and ACTIVE time
Reachable, unserved and loss stay distinct
Reset: new Runner invocation, same Compose

svg.text: Construction is inert. Explicit operations start tasks and acquire resources; cancellation waits for their actual exit.
